Vision to Reality: The Indoor Pool Transformation

Seeing is believing. Building an indoor pool is a complex feat of structural engineering, requiring deep excavation, reinforced foundations, and intricate climate control systems long before the first drop of water is added. Slide between the images below to see the dramatic transformation from a raw construction site into a breathtaking, move-in-ready aquatic sanctuary, perfectly insulated from the harsh Ontario winters.
How Much Does An Indoor Pool Cost To Build?

Because you are building both a complex structure and a pool, projects typically start at $400,000 and go as high as $2,000,000+ for advanced large turnkey indoor pools. A significant portion of this budget goes toward the specialized commercial-grade HVAC and dehumidification systems required to protect the building from the high humidity created by the pool.
What type of pool is best for an indoor environment?

Concrete, fiberglass, and vinyl liner pools can all be installed indoors. The right choice for your project depends on the available space, building size, budget, and desired custom features, as well as local permit and engineering requirements.

 
How do you prevent mold and structural rot in the indoor pool environment

Standard home ventilation systems are not designed to handle the high humidity of an indoor pool. Every indoor pool project requires careful planning, including a properly engineered dehumidification system and thoughtful building design. Together, these help maintain appropriate humidity levels and protect against mold growth and rot. 
Will my house smell like chlorine if the pool is attached?

Not when engineered correctly. We design the pool room’s HVAC system to maintain "negative air pressure." This means that when you open the door connecting your house to the pool, air flows from your house into the pool room, preventing the humid, chemical-scented air from ever entering your living space. 

 

 
How long does it take to construct an indoor pool from start to finish?

A complete custom indoor pool addition typically takes 6 to 12 months. This timeline depends on the complexity of the building structure, weather conditions during the foundation pouring, and the speed of municipal permit approvals. 
What temperature is the pool room kept at compared to the water?

The golden rule of indoor pool engineering is to keep the room's air temperature 2 to 4 degrees (Fahrenheit) warmer than the water temperature. This minimizes evaporation—which is the root cause of high humidity, heat loss, and structural moisture issues. 
Do i still need a pool cover for an indoor pool?

Yes, a pool cover is still highly recommended for an indoor pool because it completely stops massive water evaporation when the pool is not in use. By trapping the heat and moisture in the water, a cover drastically reduces your energy bills and prevents your expensive commercial dehumidification system from overworking. For luxury installations, we typically integrate an automatic retractable cover hidden beneath the deck to provide seamless daily convenience and added safety. 

 
Do I need to hire an architect, a builder, and a pool company? No. That is the exact nightmare Hipel Pools eliminates. As a turnkey general contractor, we manage the entire project in-house. You deal with one team for the architectural design, the building construction, the mechanical engineering, and the pool installation. 

Purpose Built Structural Architecture & Integration

 Building an indoor pool isn't about placing a body of water inside a room; it’s about engineering a specialized facility that flows seamlessly with your existing home. As your complete general contractor, we manage the precise structural requirements unique to indoor aquatic environments—from heavy-duty foundation footings that support massive water weight, to advanced vapor barriers and specialized insulation. We ensure the architectural design not only looks stunning and complements your property, but is structurally bulletproof, protecting the integrity of your home for decades to come. 

Master-Level Climate & Air Quality Engineering

The secret to a pristine indoor pool lies in mastering the invisible: the microclimate. Standard homebuilders often fail to account for the immense moisture an indoor pool generates, leading to foggy windows, mold, and corrosive structural damage. We engineer dehumidification and HVAC systems specifically designed for aquatic environments. By establishing perfect negative air pressure and pinpoint temperature controls, we ensure your pool room always smells fresh, the air feels perfectly breathable, and your expansive glass windows remain crystal clear, even in the dead of winter. 

The Seamless, Turnkey Construction Experience

An indoor pool is one of the most complex residential construction projects possible, usually requiring the stressful coordination of architects, HVAC engineers, foundation crews, and separate pool installers. Hipel Pools eliminates that headache entirely. As your dedicated general contractor, we are your single point of contact from the initial soil excavation to the moment you dive into warm water. We manage the municipal permits, orchestrate the specialized trades, construct the building, and install the pool. You get to focus on the exciting design finishes, while we handle the heavy lifting.
Experience Of Over 200+ Pool Builds
At Hipel Pools we've built over 200 swimming pools. We know pools inside and out and everything it takes to make a pool function. That's why our construction capabilities are like no other our experience speaks for itself.
